description:
[EPIC] Lower a multi-target protocol callsite into matrix-generated type-dispatch glue over the EXISTING impl functions. Fixes fz-9i4.7.2 without synthesizing any new function.

PROBLEM. Protocol callbacks (Enumerable.reduce, ...) are bare FunctionIds with no body (source_publish.rs:185). resolve_function_call (jobs/semantic.rs:1161) routes them to resolve_protocol_call (1224), which intersects the receiver type with each impl's module_impl_target_ty and emits ONE CallTargetSummary per overlapping impl. Concrete receiver -> 1 target -> already a plain DirectCall to the existing impl (works today). Union receiver (e.g. list|range, coarsened by convergence_collapse because Enum.* does not itself dispatch on it) -> MULTI-target -> materialize_direct_call_edge (artifact.rs:573) asserts single_target() -> fatal 'unresolved multi-target direct callsite'.

DESIGN (corrected). The selection is ALREADY computed by resolve_protocol_call and ALREADY monomorphizes: type-known -> one target -> direct call to the existing impl (NO glue, NO wrapper); type genuinely unknown (union) -> several targets. Dynamic dispatch is needed ONLY in that union case. So: KEEP resolve_protocol_call (its multi-target output is correct). The dispatch matrix (src/dispatch_matrix/) GENERATES the glue that SELECTS the existing impl by the receiver's runtime type; the leaves are direct calls to the impls that already exist. We do NOT create a dispatcher function (a synthesized callback body would route EVERY call -- even type-known ones -- through an extra frame, regressing the common case). The fix is purely: faithfully lower a multi-target CallSiteSummary instead of asserting it away.

SEAM. MaterializedCallEdge.callee is a single CallTarget<ExecutableKey> (artifact.rs:132). Grow it to host a runtime type-dispatch: a PatternDispatchPlan<Ty> over the targets' receiver-overlap types + one CallTarget per arm. Codegen already has the type-test primitive (LoweredTail::Dispatch emission: native.rs DispatchState, backend.rs:453) -- reuse it for the call edge. Thread the new shape through every call-edge stage: materialize -> AbiReadyCallEdge -> EmissionReadyCallEdge -> BackendProgram -> native. ALL return flows (Tail / Continue / Deliver).

DISCRIMINANT. Each CallTargetSummary carries surface_inputs (CallTargetSummary.surface_inputs, semantic.rs:34); input[0] is the receiver narrowed to that impl's overlap -- the per-arm type test. Build one Region::Type arm per (impl target, receiver_ty); struct-target arms ordered before the map arm (a struct value is also a map; sound for list/range without fz-bv3). The arm-row construction already prototyped in jobs/protocol_dispatch.rs (the abandoned WIP) transplants almost verbatim -- it just feeds from callsite targets and is consumed at the call edge, not as a function's entry dispatch.

PROVEN. Runtime type-dispatch over a union compiles+runs in interp AND AOT via the existing dispatch pipeline. The concrete-receiver path is already a single direct call and stays untouched.

Children: .4 remove the abandoned synthesized-dispatcher WIP; .2 build the callsite dispatch matrix from a multi-target CallSiteSummary (pure, unit-testable); .5 the cross-stage dispatch call-edge (representation + materialize + abi + emission + backend + native, all return flows) consuming .2; .3 re-enable fz-9i4.7.2 fixtures + matrix green. Separate: fz-kot (Enum.take/drop return [] even monomorphically) is independent and also needed for enum_take_drop_split correctness; fz-bv3 (sound nominal struct-vs-map dispatch) gates only map+struct fixtures. Re-verify file:line vs HEAD.

comments.text: SCOPE on struct/map soundness (fz-bv3): the Enumerable dispatcher has 3 arms (List/Map/Range). Order STRUCT arms before the MAP arm. list/range receivers (enum_take_drop_split, range_enumerable, etc.) route soundly without fz-bv3. Programs using Enum over plain MAPS together with structs/ranges need fz-bv3 (sound nominal-tag struct dispatch) -- fz-bin.3 gates those fixtures on fz-bv3.

title: [EPIC] Protocol dispatch through the dispatch matrix
